prompt:
Normalize the single contact record embedded in the user's note. Return exactly one bare JSON object with keys "name", "phone", "email", "company", "country". All five are required; each value is a string or JSON null. No other text.

Extract only the record's label/value lines. Recognize variant labels and separators (colon, equals, tab) and any line order. Split at the label separator, not at punctuation inside a value. Ignore everything around the record. Trim each value and collapse internal whitespace runs to one space. Absent lines, blank values and these case-insensitive placeholders are missing: -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD. Missing fields yield null except for the country fallback below.

Route the country line to country. Among the other record values, assign email by the presence of @ and phone by the presence of at least seven digits with no characters other than digits, spaces and + - ( ) . / after removing a leading tel: and any extension. Do not trust name or company labels when their values are swapped: if the name-side value ends in a legal suffix listed below and the company-side value does not, exchange their roles before stripping the suffix.

Country and phone:
- Normalize an explicit country to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Recognize English, Swedish and German country names, alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes regardless of case, and common aliases: UK or Great Britain → GB; Holland → NL; USA or U.S.A. → US; Türkiye → TR; Czech Republic → CZ.
- Discard a leading tel: and a trailing extension introduced by ext., ext, x, # or extension. Classify as international only if the remaining value starts with + or 00 after ignoring an opening parenthesis. Do not recognize a calling code from bare leading digits in a national number.
- International: convert initial 00 to +, remove the optional trunk marker (0), and remove spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses. Preserve the written calling code even if the explicit country disagrees. If the country line was absent, blank or a placeholder, derive country from the international calling code only if it uniquely identifies a country; shared codes such as +1 and +7 leave country null. This fallback overrides the missing-value rule only for country.
- National: remove formatting punctuation and spaces, remove one leading trunk 0, and prepend + and the calling code for the normalized country. If country is missing, return null for phone. A non-null phone uses E.164 (+ followed by calling code and national significant number, digits only after +).

Text fields:
- Email: strip surrounding angle brackets and a leading mailto: wrapper, then lowercase the whole address. Preserve the exact source character sequence apart from these operations and general whitespace normalization. Do not insert spaces, change spelling, or derive the address from the contact's name.
- Name: split at the first comma and move the part after it before the part preceding it for Last, First order. Drop leading honorifics Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, Prof, case-insensitively with or without a dot. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the remainder of each space- or hyphen-separated part.
- Company: remove one trailing legal suffix and any optional comma before it, case-insensitively. Suffixes: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Match a full suffix, including multiword forms. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the remainder of each space-separated word.
- Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics under casing; never transliterate. Comparison is NFC-normalized. Keep normalized values trimmed.

Do not obtain values from notes, signatures, email domains or company suffixes. The only inference allowed is the international-phone fallback for missing country. Emit the JSON object only.
